reason: This passage from Nehemiah 4 explicitly portrays Yahweh as protective and supportive of the Hebrew people. The text includes prayers asking God to hear their plight and return reproach upon their enemies ('Hear, O our God, that we are despised; and turn their reproach upon their own heads'). Critically, the passage states that 'God frustrated their counsel' (וַיָּפֶר הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת־עֲצָתָם) when the enemies plotted against Jerusalem, and affirms that 'Our God will fight for us' (אֱלֹהֵינוּ יִלָּחֶם לָנוּ). Throughout the account, Yahweh is depicted as an ally to the Hebrew people against their external enemies, not as antagonistic toward them.
